title: Lecture 9 — latches and flip-flops
summary: Move from combinational logic to stored state: feedback, latch polarity, transparent intervals, clock edges and clean clock signals.
body:
This guide uses the retained lecture deck. The current Canvas lecture listing and weekly planner were checked on 21 September and confirm this lecture's scheduled date and topic; the full PDF has not been redownloaded and actual classroom coverage is not a transcript. No attendance or completion is inferred.

The central question is when a circuit is allowed to change its remembered value. First trace an SR latch with feedback, then distinguish a D latch's transparent interval from a flip-flop's sampling edge. Use the examples to follow the same input history through both devices. Finally connect the storage rule to registers, enables, reset and a clock divider.

The saved deck also explains why switch bounce matters in the lab and recommends a two-button latch clock for Labs 3 and 4. Read the current lab instructions before building; conceptual preparation is separate from completed laboratory work. The worked examples and self-checks below are newly authored practice.
